questions.q: Why did David want to show covenant faithfulness to anyone left in Saul’s house?
questions.a: David wanted to show covenant faithfulness for the sake of Jonathan.

questions.q: How did Ziba answer the king when he was asked if anyone was left in Saul’s house?
questions.a: Ziba told the king that one son of Jonathan was still alive but not able to walk.

questions.q: Who was left in Saul’s house?
questions.a: Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, was left.

questions.q: What kindness did David show Mephibosheth for Jonathan’s sake?
questions.a: David restored to Mephibosheth all the land of his grandfather Saul, and he had Mephibosheth eat meals with his family continually.

questions.q: What did David tell Ziba to do for Mephibosheth?
questions.a: David told Ziba that he, his sons, and his servants were to work the land for Mephibosheth and bring in the harvest.

questions.q: Where did Mephibosheth live after David showed him kindness?
questions.a: Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem because he ate meals with David’s family in the palace.

questions.q: What physical problem did Mephibosheth have?
questions.a: Mephibosheth was lame in both of his feet.

commentary.text: Verses 1–8 Amidst numerous affairs we are apt to forget the gratitude we owe, and the engagements we are under, not only to our friends, but to God himself. Yet persons of real godliness will have no rest till they have discharged them. And the most proper objects of kindness and charity, frequently will not be found without inquiry. Jonathan was David's sworn friend, therefore he shows kindness to his son Mephibosheth. God is faithful to us; let us not be unfaithful to one another. If Providence has raised us, and our friends and their families are brought low, we must look upon that as giving us the fairer opportunity of being kind to them.

As David was a type of Christ, his Lord and Son, his Root and Offspring, let his kindness to Mephibosheth remind us of the kindness and love of God our Saviour to fallen man, to whom he was under no obligation, as David was to Jonathan. The Son of God seeks this lost and ruined race, who sought not after him. He comes to seek and to save them!
